record.original_question: Can one characterize exactly which subcubic K3-free graphs are Class 2? Equivalently, is it possible to describe all K3-free graphs of maximum degree at most 3 whose chromatic index is 4 rather than their maximum degree?

evidence.quote: It is known that subdividing a single edge of a 3-edge colorable cubic graph yields an overfull subcubic graph G. Hence, G is of Class 2, i.e., chi'(G) = 4. Starting with a K3-free cubic graph, we produce, in that way, a K3-free subcubic graph of Class 2.
This raises the following question: Problem 6.1 Is it possible to describe all subcubic K3-free graphs of Class 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is called subcubic if its maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ is at most $3$, and $K_3$-free (triangle-free) if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices. The chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ is the minimum number of colors needed to color the edges of $G$ so that no two edges sharing an endpoint receive the same color. By Vizing's theorem, every graph satisfies $\chi'(G) \in \{\Delta(G), \Delta(G)+1\}$; a graph is said to be of Class 1 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)$ and of Class 2 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)+1$.

Provide a structural characterization of all subcubic $K_3$-free graphs that are of Class 2. Equivalently, describe all triangle-free graphs $G$ with $\Delta(G) \le 3$ for which $\chi'(G) = 4$.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the chromatic index of triangle-free subcubic graphs is known to be NP-complete (Koreas, 1997), so a simple characterization seems unlikely. No structural characterization of Class 2 subcubic triangle-free graphs appears in the literature; the problem is generally treated as open.

status_evidence.title: The NP-completeness of chromatic index in triangle free graphs with maximum vertex of degree 3
status_evidence.snippet: Edge-coloring is NP-complete even when restricted to triangle-free graphs of maximum degree 3.
status_evidence.claim: Deciding Class 1 vs Class 2 for subcubic triangle-free graphs is NP-complete, indicating no easy characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Edge coloring - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: By Vizing's theorem, the chromatic index is either Δ or Δ+1; classifying graphs as Class 1 or Class 2 is generally hard.
status_evidence.claim: No general characterization of Class 2 graphs is known, even within restricted classes.
